keyword: how long will it take the astronauts to get to the moon

verifications.claim: Astronauts on the Artemis II mission are expected to take approximately four to five days to reach the Moon's vicinity, according to USA Today and CBS News.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly a four-day journey to the far side of the moon'; R5: 'reaching the moon's vicinity around day five or six'; R3: 'get to the moon on the sixth day'
verifications.reasoning: R1 (CBS) and R5 (USA Today) directly support ~4-5 days after initial orbit, aligning with total ~5 days to vicinity; R3 confirms day 6.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will spend about 24 hours in Earth orbit before conducting a trans-lunar injection to boost them on a path to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'spend their first 24 hours or so in orbit around the Earth... Then... "trans-lunar injection," or TLI'; R5: 'first one to two days... translunar injection burn on day two'; R3: 'orbit Earth in the days following launch... “translunar injection burn,”... on the second day'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state ~24 hours or 1-2 days in Earth orbit before TLI.

verifications.claim: The entire Artemis II crewed flight is expected to last about 10 days, according to NASA and CNN.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'mission is slated to last about nine and a half days'; R5: '10-day expedition... expected to last about 10 days'; R6: 'overall mission around the Moon and back expected to take about 10 days'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently state ~10 days total mission duration, attributed to NASA in contexts.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II spacecraft is expected to fly by the Moon around day five or six of the mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'reaching the moon's vicinity around day five or six'; R3: 'get to the moon on the sixth day... make one pass around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: R5 exactly matches 'day five or six'; R3 specifies day 6 for arrival and flyby.

verifications.claim: Apollo 8 reached the Moon in just under three days, according to NASA and Sky at Night Magazine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'fastest Apollo mission (Apollo 8) took 69 hours and 8 minutes'; R4: 'just under three days'; R2: '2 days 20 hours'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm Apollo 8 reached Moon in ~3 days or less (69-76 hours).

verifications.claim: The Apollo 8 trip to the Moon was the fastest, according to NASA and Sky at Night Magazine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'The fastest Apollo mission (Apollo 8)'; R4: 'The fastest of these was Apollo 8'
verifications.reasoning: R6 explicitly calls Apollo 8 the fastest; R4 confirms among Apollo missions.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trajectory is designed for safety and system testing, according to NASA and Sky at Night Magazine.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'check out the Orion capsule, making sure... systems are working properly before heading to the moon'; R5: 'test life support systems and critical operations'; R6: 'Crewed missions tend to take longer... expected to take the Artemis II mission about four days'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe testing and longer trajectory for crewed missions implying safety, but R6 less explicit on 'designed for safety and system testing'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trajectory takes slightly longer than Apollo 8's, according to NASA and Sky at Night Magazine.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'The fastest Apollo mission (Apollo 8) took 69 hours... Artemis II mission about four days'
verifications.reasoning: R6 directly compares Apollo 8 (~3 days) to Artemis II (~4 days), showing longer time.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will not orbit the Moon, according to NBC Chicago.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'never entering low-lunar orbit... one pass around the moon'; R1: 'will not... go into lunar orbit. Instead... loop around it'
verifications.reasoning: R3 (NBC) explicitly states no low-lunar orbit, just pass around.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will not land on the Moon, according to NBC Chicago.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: context of no landing implied in flyby description; R1: 'will not land on the moon'; R5: 'The crew will not land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: R3 describes flyby without landing; other sources explicit.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will perform a flyby of the Moon, according to NBC Chicago.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'make one pass around the moon'; R5: 'lunar flyby'; R1: 'loop around it'
verifications.reasoning: R3 describes pass around Moon, matching flyby.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will return to Earth on a free-return trajectory, according to NBC Chicago.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'use the gravity of Earth to be drawn back toward the planet'; R1: '"free return" trajectory'; R5: 'free-return trajectory around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: R3 describes gravity-assisted return matching free-return concept, though phrasing 'gravity of Earth' slightly imprecise; others explicit.
